title: Move drinks away from a keyboard and phone
instruction: Move both drinks at least 15 cm away from the keyboard and the phone, without moving the keyboard or the phone.
context: A drink spilled on a keyboard or phone shorts it out; office and lab rules keep liquids away from equipment.
setup: A keyboard (30 x 9 x 2.4 cm, 0.5 kg) lies left to right on the table 33 cm in front of the arm bases, centred on their midline. A smartphone (14 x 6.6 x 1.1 cm, 0.17 kg) lies 21 cm in front of the bases, 10 cm right of the midline. A red ceramic mug (8.5 cm across with its handle, 6 cm tall, 0.3 kg) stands 1.6 cm from the keyboard's left end, and a takeaway coffee cup (6.5 cm wide, 10 cm tall, 0.25 kg) 1.2 cm from the phone's right side.
scoring: 0 if a drink ever tilts more than 30 degrees (spilled), or if the keyboard or phone ends more than 2 cm from its start. Otherwise 0.5 for each drink that stands upright (within 15 degrees) with at least 15 cm between its outline and the outlines of both the keyboard and the phone, measured horizontally edge to edge.
reset_notes: Stand the drinks back on their marks next to the keyboard and phone.
fidelity: Rigid bodies only; the drinks hold no liquid, so a tilt past 30 degrees counts as a spill. Every surface has the same rubber-like friction (1.2), so a pushed cup tips rather than slides.
